Article Title: India’s exports to US, China surge in August amid stronger global trade
Article Text:
India’s exports to the US rise 21.8%, China shipments jump 52.4% in August (representative image)

US exports rise despite higher tariffs

China shipments climb over 52%

Singapore exports jump 161%

Overall exports rise 26.12% in August

Imports from Oman, Taiwan and Brazil surge

India’s merchandise exports to the US and China recorded strong growth in August 2026, with shipments to the US rising 21.83% and those to China increasing 52.35% from a year earlier, according to commerce ministry data released on Tuesday.Exports to the US rose to $8.4 billion during the month, while shipments to China increased to $1.9 billion.Imports from both countries also grew during August, with inbound shipments from China rising 17% to $12.77 billion and those from the US jumping 65.78% to $5.97 billion.During April-August 2026-27, India’s merchandise exports to the US grew 6.17% to $42.8 billion, while imports from the country increased 29.6% to $28 billion.India and the US are currently negotiating a trade pact. The US imposed an additional 10% tariff on Indian goods from July 24.Despite the tariff-related trade measures, exports to the US recorded year-on-year growth in August.India’s exports to China rose 38.71% during April-August 2026-27 to $9.64 billion, while imports from China increased 27% to $65.5 billion, according to the Commerce Ministry data.The August figures showed an even sharper rise in exports to China, with shipments increasing 52.35% year-on-year to $1.9 billion.China remained a major source of imports, with India’s inbound shipments from the country reaching $12.77 billion in August.India also recorded a sharp increase in exports to Singapore during August. Shipments rose 160.96% year-on-year to $1.9 billion.During the first five months of the fiscal year, exports to Singapore jumped 96.56% to $9.5 billion.Exports to Germany, South Africa, Tanzania, Australia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and Italy also recorded positive growth during August.However, shipments to some major markets declined. Exports to the UAE fell 26.1% to $2.4 billion, which the commerce ministry attributed to the West Asia crisis.Exports to the Netherlands and Saudi Arabia also declined during the month.India’s overall merchandise exports rose 26.12% year-on-year to $43.81 billion in August, driven by higher shipments of electronics, engineering goods and petroleum products.Electronics exports increased 90%, engineering goods exports rose 25% and petroleum product shipments climbed 63.27% during the month.Merchandise imports rose 14.1% to $70.76 billion, with higher imports of crude oil, project goods, electronic items, silver, coal and coke.Gold imports fell 57.75% to $2.3 billion in August, helping narrow the merchandise trade deficit to $26.86 billion, its lowest level in five months.The August export growth was the highest since June 2022, when shipments had increased 30.12%.During April-August 2026-27, merchandise exports rose 17.85% to $215.91 billion, while imports increased 18.21% to $363 billion. The merchandise trade deficit for the first five months stood at $147.09 billion, compared with $123.88 billion in the corresponding period last year.India also recorded higher imports from Russia, South Korea, Singapore, Germany, Oman, Malaysia, Taiwan and Brazil during August.Imports from Oman surged 157.45% to $1.64 billion, while those from Taiwan rose 108.31% to $1.6 billion. Imports from Brazil increased 132% to $1.12 billion.Crude oil imports rose 37.28% to about $16 billion in August. During April-August, crude oil imports increased to $95.57 billion from $78.07 billion a year earlier.Electronic goods imports during the first five months rose to $66.48 billion from $46.31 billion. In August, electronics and project goods imports grew 53.27% to $13 billion and 377.71% to $960.78 million, respectively.Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal described the August numbers as robust.“These numbers reaffirm the growing strength and competitiveness of our manufacturing ecosystem, with our exporters expanding India's footprint across global markets,” he said in a social media post.Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said export growth momentum was continuing and “rather, building up also”. He said higher imports during the first five months were being driven by domestic economic expansion, rising energy requirements and critical inputs needed for manufacturing growth.Services exports were estimated at $38.87 billion in August, while services imports stood at $21.42 billion.
Article Summary: India’s exports to the US rise 21.8%, China shipments jump 52.4% in August. Inbound shipments from China rising 17% to $12.77 billion and those from the US jumping 65.78%. India also recorded a sharp increase in exports to Singapore during August. Overall exports rise 26.12% year-on-year to $43.81 billion.

Article Title: UPI payments up to Rs 2,000 to remain free of charges: Govt
Article Text:
UPI payments. (Representative image)

Government on Monday notified that banks and payment system providers cannot impose direct or indirect charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to Rs 2,000 or payments made using RuPay debit cards.The notification was issued under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.“In exercise of the powers conferred by section 10 A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (51 of 2007), the Central Government hereby specifies the following electronic modes of payment, namely: (i) Debit Card powered by RuPay; and (ii) Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions upto Rs. 2,000,” the ministry of finance said.“No bank or system provider shall impose, whether directly or indirectly, any charge upon a person making or receiving a payment by using the electronic modes of payment specified in paragraph above,” it added.The notification keeps UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 free of charges and paves the way for a possible nominal Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on selected UPI merchant transactions above a specified threshold.The government had indicated in August that consumers and person-to-person payments would continue to remain free. Any fee, if introduced, would be paid by merchants rather than consumers, government officials said, according to Reuters.The government said the proposed changes were part of a broader effort to make India’s digital payments ecosystem sustainable, competitive and capable of supporting the country’s growing digital economy.The finance ministry also rejected reports that external influences were behind the proposed policy changes, describing such claims as “unfounded, completely false and misleading.”Launched a decade ago, UPI processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 trillion in August. Google Pay and Walmart-owned PhonePe accounted for around three-fourths of the month’s total UPI transaction volume.
Article Summary: Government on Monday notified that banks and payment system providers cannot impose direct or indirect charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to Rs 2,000. The notification was issued under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. UPI processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 trillion in August.

Article Title: 100% tariffs on India? US House advances Russia sanctions bill; final vote tomorrow
Article Text:
The bill is aimed at putting further economic pressure on Moscow by targeting countries that continue to trade in Russian oil and gas. The US has argued that revenue from Russia's crude oil trade helps fund its war against Ukraine.

What the bill means for India

House vote shocks Democrats

What happens next

The US House of Representatives on Tuesday advanced a bill that could allow US President Donald Trump to impose 100 per cent tariffs on India and other major buyers of Russian oil and gas, bringing the measure closer to becoming law. The bill also seeks to extend sanctions on Russia and Iran.The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 cleared a key procedural vote by 214-211, with two Democrats joining Republicans in backing the measure. The House is expected to hold a final vote on the bill on Wednesday.For India, the bill is significant because it could give Trump the authority to impose punitive tariffs on countries that continue buying Russian energy. India is among Russia's major oil buyers and has sharply increased its purchases of discounted Russian crude since the Ukraine war began.The Senate had already passed the bill on August 7 by an overwhelming 86-11 vote. The Senate version does not specifically name India or China. Instead, it refers to the five largest importers of Russian oil and gas by volume.If the House passes the bill, it will have to be sent to Trump for his signature before it can become law.The proposed measure could expose Indian exports to the US to tariffs of up to 100 per cent if Trump uses the authority against countries buying Russian energy.The bill is aimed at putting further economic pressure on Moscow by targeting countries that continue to trade in Russian oil and gas. The US has argued that revenue from Russia's crude oil trade helps fund its war against Ukraine.The measure would also target Russia's leadership and energy sector, along with the "shadow fleet" of vessels used to transport Russian oil and evade sanctions.The potential tariff threat comes as India continues to balance its energy needs and its ties with both Russia and the US.The procedural vote was approved 214-211 after two Democratic lawmakers broke ranks and voted with Republicans, a move that reportedly shocked House Democratic leadership.Democratic Congressman Gregory Meeks, the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, had opposed the legislation on Monday. He argued that it would give Trump broad powers to impose tariffs without sufficient safeguards.The bill is now expected to face a final House vote on Wednesday.The timing is also significant as pro-Ukraine groups have intensified lobbying efforts in Washington.The Ukraine Action Summit, organised by the American Coalition for Ukraine, is currently being held in Washington to lobby US lawmakers for continued support for Kyiv.The House is due to break for an early recess on Thursday and is expected to reconvene on November 9 after the US midterm elections.The immediate focus is therefore on Wednesday's vote. If the House approves the legislation, it will move to the next stage of the lawmaking process and could eventually reach Trump's desk.
Article Summary: The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 cleared a key procedural vote by 214-211, with two Democrats joining Republicans in backing the measure. The House is expected to hold a final vote on the bill on Wednesday. For India, the bill is significant because it could give Trump the authority to impose punitive tariffs.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude falls as US crude inventories rise despite Saudi supply concerns
Article Text: Oil prices fell on Wednesday after an unexpected increase in US crude inventories outweighed concerns over supply disruptions following an attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline.Brent crude futures declined 93 cents, or 0.86%, to $107.82 a barrel at 0028 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped 97 cents, or 0.92%, to $104.86 a barrel.Both benchmarks had risen more than $3 on Tuesday to their highest levels since May 19 after Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at its Red Sea export hub of Yanbu and cut some shipments to Europe.US crude, gasoline and distillate inventories all increased last week, according to data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), cited by market sources.Crude inventories rose by 7.1 million barrels in the week ended September 11, against analysts’ expectations of a decline of around 1.6 million barrels, according to a Reuters poll.Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at Yanbu after shutting its East-West pipeline following an attack by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis on Friday.The pipeline is used to reroute around 4 million barrels of oil per day to the Red Sea port, equivalent to nearly 4% of global supply.The US energy secretary said oil flows through the vital pipeline should resume within days. However, sources told Reuters that repairs could take five to six weeks, while partial pumping could resume sooner.The disruption has also affected Saudi oil shipments to Europe, intensifying concerns over global supplies. In a separate development unrelated to the Iran conflict, Libya’s National Oil Corporation said operations at three oil fields had been suspended.The disruption occurred after protesting members of the Petroleum Facilities Guard shut a valve on the Hamada-Zawiya crude export pipeline.Shipping concerns have also increased after commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to fewer than 10 transits a day over the weekend, compared with a 10-day average of 14.The waterway carried nearly one-fifth of global oil supplies before the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28.Planned discussions between Gulf Arab states and Iran were also postponed, raising concerns that the regional conflict could widen and further disrupt energy shipments.Asian stocks made tentative gains on Wednesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision later in the day.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fluctuated between gains and losses after falling for four consecutive sessions. It was last up 0.2%, led by a 0.8% rise in South Korean shares. S&P 500 e-mini futures edged up 0.1%.
Article Summary: US crude, gasoline and distillate inventories all increased last week. Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at Yanbu after shutting its East-West pipeline. Libya’s National Oil Corporation said operations at three oil fields had been suspended. Asian stocks made tentative gains on Wednesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision.

Article Title: UPI charges from October 15: 0.4% MDR on payments above Rs 2,000, but flat Rs 5 fee for railway tickets, fuel, insurance and utilities; sending money to friends, family, Autopay for OTT stays free
Article Text:
The MDR will have to be borne by merchants. Larger retailers, online platforms and restaurants, among others, may choose to absorb the cost.

If you are still wondering what transactions will be subject to what charge, we break it down for you:

UPI Transactions: What Remains Free

Flat MDR for These UPI Transactions:

Capital Market transactions made through UPI

Insurance Premium

Fuel purchased at petrol pumps

Electricity & Water Bills

Education fees

The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Tuesday announced a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, subject to an overall cap of Rs 300. For utility payments, fuel purchases, insurance premiums, rail tickets and several government services, a flat charge of Rs 5 will apply.The MDR will have to be borne by merchants. Larger retailers, online platforms and restaurants, among others, may choose to absorb the cost. Cash transactions, meanwhile, also involve expenses, with several banks charging fees for cash deposits.The new MDR will take effect from October 15. However, UPI payments between individuals, including transfers made to friends, will continue to remain outside the charge. Auto-debits and UPI mandates will also not attract MDR.“Banks have been advised to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application provide­rs are expressly prohibited fr­om imposing platform fees or hidden charges,” the finance ministry said in a statement.All Person-to-Person Transactions: UPI transfers made directly between individuals will continue to be completely free, regardless of the amount involved.Individuals will not be charged a transaction fee, platform fee or any other fee for sending or receiving money through UPI. As a result, transactions between individuals, which account for 70% of the total UPI transaction value, will remain outside the MDR framework.Merchant Payments Up to Rs 2,000: Person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI payments of up to Rs 2,000 will not attract MDR.Payments Received by Small Merchants: Small merchants, including street vendors, who receive up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to get zero MDR on all their transactions. This will ensure that street vendors, neighbourhood shops and other small businesses do not face additional costs for accepting digital payments.Certain merchant categories, including railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, among others, will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5 for transactions above Rs 2,000. Unlike the 0.4% variable rate, these sectors will pay a fixed Rs 5 per transaction irrespective of the transaction value. So if you are paying for a railway ticket via UPI, it does not attract 0.4% MDR but Rs 5 which again is not borne by you but the merchant.The flat-fee structure is intended to prevent transaction costs from rising in critical public services, utility bill collection and low-margin sectors such as fuel retail. It also keeps essential consumer services digitally efficient and low-cost.UPI transactions related to the capital market, including payments for mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers, will attract an MDR of 0.02% of the transaction value, subject to a maximum charge of Rs 300.This rate is lower than the standard rates applicable to commercial transactions and is intended to encourage retail participation in the formal financial market.The Capital Market MDR category covers regulated entities operating in the capital markets, including Asset Management Companies (Mutual Funds), SEBI-registered stockbrokers, securities dealers and investment platforms.The framework applies to UPI fund transfers made for equity purchases, debt market investments, mutual fund purchases and broker wallet top-ups. By placing these transactions in a separate category, capital market payments are distinguished from regular retail purchases and general service payments.Insurance premiums paid through UPI are covered under a concessional flat-rate structure. For insurance payments above Rs 2,000, the MDR is fixed at Rs 5 per transaction instead of being calculated as a percentage of the payment amount.UPI payments for fuel purchases above Rs 2,000 at petrol stations will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5. The fixed charge is intended to prevent petrol pump operators from facing higher processing costs on larger fuel purchases.For fuel payments below Rs 2,000, the MDR will remain at 0%.Public utility payments, including electricity bills, municipal water charges and piped natural gas payments, fall under the designated Industry program category. For payments above Rs 2,000, a concessional flat MDR of Rs 5 will apply instead of the 0.4% variable rate.Utility bill payments below Rs 2,000 will continue to carry zero MDR.Recurring auto-debit payments such as utility bills, OTT subscriptionsAutomated recurring payments made through standing instructions, known as UPI Mandates or AutoPay, do not attract the prescribed MDR transaction charges.As a result, recurring payments set up through automated transfers, including monthly utility bills, OTT streaming subscriptions and recurring investments, will not incur the prescribed MDR charge on the transaction.Educational fee payments, such as school tuition, university term fees and institutional entrance examination charges, are covered under the designated Industry program category. Payments above Rs 2,000 will benefit from flat-fee structures or capped processing rates, rather than being subjected to high percentage-based charges on larger fee amounts.Educational payments up to Rs 2,000 will remain completely free of MDR.
Article Summary: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Tuesday announced a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. For utility payments, fuel purchases, insurance premiums, rail tickets and several government services, a flat charge of Rs 5 will apply. Larger retailers, online platforms and restaurants, among others, may choose to absorb the cost.

This oil-driven inflation scare, combined with hot US PPI data, sent gold sliding to a more than one-month low, with spot prices testing $4,253 on Monday, down more than 3% for the month and nearly 10% from August's highs of $4,696.The sell-off deepened as the 10-year US Treasury yield broke through the psychologically important 5% mark, briefly touching 5.04%, its highest level since 2007, sharply raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.The hawkish shift was reinforced by expectations building into Wednesday's Fed meeting, with swaps now pricing in a 92-95% probability of a 25-basis-point hike, a sharp jump from just a week ago. Article Title: Rooftop solar market has potential to reach 132 GW by 2030: ISMA
Article Text:
ISMA has projected that India’s rooftop solar market has the potential to scale to 132 GW from the current 17 GW installed capacity

Market Sizing and Growth Outlook

NEW DELHI: Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA) has projected that India’s rooftop solar market has the potential to scale to 132 GW from the current 17 GW installed capacity, with an annual demand outlook ranging between 9-15 GW till 2030.In its report on the residential rooftop solar market, titled, ISMA said this will also create demand for domestically manufactured components, including solar cells, modules, inverters and balance-of-system components.ISMA’s assessment is based on national residential electricity consumption, household housing characteristics and distribution utility tariffs.The report also highlighted the “affordability effect”, showing that rooftop solar adoption is increasingly expanding beyond states where its economics are naturally strongest. Govt’s flagship scheme, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, has helped bring rooftop solar within reach of households across larger residential markets, demonstrating the role of policy support in broadening adoption and creating a more sustained demand base for India’s domestic solar manufacturing ecosystem.Launched in Feb 2024, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY) aims to bring rooftop solar to one crore Indian homes by March 2027.The total number of rooftop solar installations has reached 47.8 lakh with total installed capacity of 16.8 GW, benefitting nearly 56.9 lakh families. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has so far disbursed over Rs 31,515 crore as central financial assistance, while several states are also running separate subsidy schemes to promote the installation of rooftop solar systems.ISMA general secretary Amit Manohar said the PM Surya Ghar scheme has played an important role in expanding residential rooftop solar adoption, particularly in markets where project economics remain challenging. “As the current programme approaches the March 2027 deadline, providing early clarity on its next phase, including consideration of PM Surya Ghar 2.0, preferably by December 2026, would help maintain market continuity and provide greater visibility to consumers and industry stakeholders,” said Manohar.The report noted that policy continuity beyond March 2027 will be important to sustain demand and provide manufacturers and other stakeholders with the visibility required to plan investments, capacity expansion and domestic supply chains.
Article Summary: Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA) has projected that India’s rooftop solar market has the potential to scale to 132 GW from the current 17 GW installed capacity. ISMA said this will also create demand for domestically manufactured components, including solar cells, modules, inverters and balance- of-system components.

Article Title: Paytm shares surge over 7% after 0.4% MDR on UPI payments above Rs 2,000
Article Text: Shares of fintech companies, including Paytm, rallied in early trade on Wednesday after the government announced a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments above Rs 2,000 made to merchants, effective October 15.Shares of One97 Communications Ltd, which owns the Paytm brand, rose 7.24% during intraday trade to hit a 52-week high of Rs 1,856.50 on the BSE. One Mobikwik Systems gained 5.96%, while Pine Labs advanced 2.68%.However, the gains later weakened. Pine Labs was trading nearly 7% lower, while One Mobikwik Systems declined around 2%.The domestic equity markets opened higher on Wednesday, recovering from the previous session’s sharp sell-off. The gains came ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s September 15–16 policy meeting, despite elevated US bond yields and high crude oil prices.The BSE Sensex opened at 74,249.31, compared with the previous close of 74,003.82. It later rose to around 74,388.37, gaining 384.55 points, or 0.52%.The NSE Nifty opened at 23,201.60 against the previous close of 23,118.60. It was trading at around 23,244.30, up 125.70 points, or 0.54%.By 1:22 pm, the Sensex had gained 425.55 points, or 0.58%, to trade at 74,429.37. The Nifty 50 was up 139.50 points, or 0.60%, at 23,258.35 at 1:23 pm.At around 9:29 am, Paytm shares were trading at Rs 1,767.05, up Rs 35.95, or 2.08%. One Mobikwik Systems was quoted at Rs 203.90, higher by Rs 1.95, or 0.97%.Most sectoral indices traded in the green, although Nifty Realty, Consumer Durables and Healthcare remained under pressure. Most broader market indices also traded higher.In the commodities market, Brent crude was trading at around $108.06 per barrel, while crude oil was quoted at approximately $104.69 per barrel. Gold was trading at around $4,326.65.The government’s decision marks a shift after nearly six years of fully free UPI payments. Under the new framework, a 0.4% MDR will apply to person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The charge will be capped at Rs 300 for transactions worth Rs 75,000 or more.Everyday person-to-person (P2P) payments and small merchant transactions will remain free. “Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI,” the finance ministry said in a statement.“MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments,” it added.Individuals will also continue to have “unlimited free usage, with no monthly quotas, volume restrictions or tiered caps on free UPI transactions”, the ministry said.Paytm said the new framework would generate additional revenue from merchant transactions that were previously free. “This will generate additional revenue from the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free earlier,” Paytm said in a regulatory filing late on Tuesday.According to an NPCI circular, customers would not be charged for UPI payments, which would continue to remain free, the company added.
Article Summary: Shares of One97 Communications Ltd, which owns the Paytm brand, rose 7.24% during intraday trade to hit a 52-week high of Rs 1,856.50 on the BSE. One Mobikwik Systems gained 5.96%, while Pine Labs advanced 2.68%. However, the gains later weakened. Pine Labs was trading nearly 7% lower, while One Mobkwik Systems declined around 2%.

Article Title: Oracle begins cutting jobs, 3,000 may face the axe in India taking workforce to 27,000; routine Indian IT sector roles face pressure even as GCC hiring is set to grow 9-10%
Article Text:
The latest Oracle cuts come against the backdrop of similar workforce reductions

Oracle Layoffs

GCC hiring trends

Oracle has reportedly started another round of job cuts globally, with industry experts tracking the company estimating that around 10% of its India workforce, or roughly 3,000 employees, could be affected.The company had already eliminated 21,000 jobs earlier this year, including around 12,000 positions in India, as it shifted its focus and spending towards AI infrastructure.Pareekh Jain, chief executive of market intelligence firm EIIRTrend, said the latest reductions could bring Oracle's India employee count down to about 27,000 from 30,000. According to Jain, the company's recruitment for AI-related roles is unlikely to offset the job losses because “new hiring in AI will be in small numbers and on a case-by-case basis”.Reports of the layoffs have also surfaced on X and Reddit, where some users identifying themselves as Oracle employees in India discussed the job cuts.Some said they were given little advance notice before being informed that their positions had been eliminated.One user shared what was described as an Oracle termination email, saying the date on which it was received was also their final working day. Another person claiming to have spent 10 years with the company said they had received an email informing them that they no longer “fit the bill”.The latest Oracle cuts come against the backdrop of similar workforce reductions at several large global capability centres (GCCs), as multinational parent companies trim employee numbers across their international operations.ET had earlier reported that Visa reduced its India workforce by around 1,500, PayPal cut 500-600 jobs and ServiceNow eliminated a few hundred positions.Jain estimates that layoffs currently account for around 1% of the overall GCC workforce.Despite these reductions, India's GCC sector is still expected to add employees overall. Industry estimates indicate that GCC employment could increase by 9-10% this year as new centres are established and existing operations expand.The more significant shift, however, is in the type of technology professionals these centres are seeking as their hiring requirements evolve.Global Capability Centres, the specialised offshore operations of multinational companies, are increasingly drawing employees away from the traditional IT services sector.A recent PwC report on GCCs says these centres have moved well beyond their earlier role of handling transactional back-office work. They are now involved in shaping enterprise strategy and outcomes across areas such as advanced analytics, product engineering, cybersecurity, AI research and development, and, increasingly, global P&L mandates.This shift is making GCCs a more significant source of technology hiring in India. As companies move beyond operations built primarily around cost savings, their requirements are expanding towards technology, innovation and enterprise transformation, pushing up demand for specialised talent.Demand for professionals with artificial intelligence-related skills is also rising, experts said. The PwC report found that the strongest requirement is for people who can build AI models, create the data infrastructure that supports them, manage associated risks, secure their deployment and turn these technologies into products and platforms that produce measurable business outcomes.The biggest opportunity lies at the mid-career level, where GCCs are looking for professionals who bring both technical expertise and an understanding of business. At the senior level, hiring is more focused on specialised roles such as architects, AI leaders, product leaders and cybersecurity and cloud specialists, experts said.The challenge, however, is that the availability of such talent is limited. GCCs require niche skills, and the gap between demand and supply remains significant.According to the PwC report, the biggest constraint for GCCs is finding professionals who possess deep domain knowledge alongside advanced technology capabilities.Competition for this talent is also intense. GCCs are competing with other GCCs, IT services companies and startups for the same limited pool of professionals. At the same time, there is a shortage of senior leaders with the strategic capabilities needed in the AI era.“This supply-side challenge is multi-layered and self-perpetuating. Acquiring AI-ready talent is becoming increasingly difficult, driven by scarce specialised capabilities, leadership gaps, and intense market competition,” the PwC report says.“The hybrid, senior, AI-fluent talent with domain expertise that India’s GCC ecosystem needs most is hardest to find, most expensive to acquire, and most fiercely competed for across the market,” it adds.
Article Summary: Oracle has reportedly started another round of job cuts globally. Around 10% of its India workforce, or roughly 3,000 employees, could be affected. The company had already eliminated 21,000 jobs earlier this year, including around 12,000 positions in India.

Article Title: 'To strengthen UPI's long-term sustainability': RBI backs 0.4% MDR on transactions above Rs 2,000
Article Text:
The RBI said the move would help UPI "continue to scale, innovate and serve consumers."

No UPI charges for customers

How much will merchants pay?

NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India has backed the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on large-value UPI transactions, saying the move would help strengthen the long-term sustainability of India’s digital payments ecosystem.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has notified an MDR of 0.4% on person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, with the new charges set to take effect from October 15, 2026. Person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free.The RBI said the move would help UPI “continue to scale, innovate and serve consumers and businesses across the country”.“It will help UPI in continuing to scale, innovate and serve consumers and businesses across the country,” the RBI said in a post on X on Tuesday.The government has clarified that the new MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem and will not be directly imposed on customers.“Customers will not be required to pay any charge when making such payments through UPI,” the finance ministry said in a statement quoting the NPCI circular issued on Tuesday.“MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments,” the statement added.The RBI said all UPI transactions, both P2P and P2M, will remain free for users. P2M transactions of up to Rs 2,000 will also continue to remain free for merchants.Under the new structure, merchants will pay an MDR of 0.4% on P2M UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. For transactions of Rs 75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction.MDR is essentially a fee charged to merchants for accepting digital payments through a particular channel. It is generally calculated as a percentage of the transaction value, with the applicable amount deducted before the remaining payment is transferred to the merchant.The new rates will come into effect on October 15, giving acquiring banks, payment aggregators, fintech companies and corporate accounting platforms time to update their software and billing systems.There will be no impact on UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000, which account for more than 95% of P2M UPI transactions by volume.The government has said the move is intended to keep everyday digital payments free while creating a sustainable revenue model for the UPI ecosystem.The RBI said a fair distribution of MDR among different participants in the payments ecosystem would support continued investment in technology, infrastructure and payment acceptance networks.“This, in turn, can enable wider UPI acceptance, deepen the customer base and support sustained growth in transaction volumes,” the RBI said.“RBI remains committed to ensuring that UPI continues to be safe, seamless, affordable, and accessible, while supporting the long-term sustainability and growth of India's world-class digital payments ecosystem,” it added.UPI is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), an initiative of the RBI and the Indian Banks’ Association. The platform enables real-time transfers between individuals and payments directly to merchants.UPI is now accepted in 11 countries, with Uzbekistan the latest addition. The other countries are Singapore, the UAE, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Greece.
Article Summary: The Reserve Bank of India has backed the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on large-value UPI transactions. The move would help strengthen the long-term sustainability of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The government has clarified that the new MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem and will not be imposed on customers.

Article Title: Revoked Slack, 4-6am emails: Oracle’s second layoff round hits India
Article Text: Bengaluru: Oracle employees have come to dread the 4am-to-6am emails and revoked Slack access.A viral Reddit post capturing the anxiety around the tech giant’s latest global layoffs simply read, “Time of death: 4 A.M. Lol.” The employee said being logged out of Slack effectively confirmed the layoff.Employees who checked Slack saw the number of active users fall to 144,638 on Tuesday around 9pm IST from 149,900 a day earlier, suggesting that more than 5,000 employees globally may have lost access over two days, sources told TOI.Employees, including those in India, have been bracing for termination emails arriving in the early hours as the latest round of cuts gets underway.Oracle began a fresh round of layoffs in India on Monday, affecting several mid- to senior-level employees in web development and maintenance, people familiar with the matter said. Some sources estimated that 1,000-1,500 employees in India could be affected, though TOI could not independently verify the figure. An email sent to Oracle did not receive a response before this article went to press. TOI also could not independently verify the number of layoffs within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) in India.Earlier this year, TOI reported that an estimated 10,000-12,000 employees in India, out of its workforce of over 40,000, were affected in the first leg of the layoffs.An email to an affected India employee said the company was streamlining operations following organisational changes and that the employee’s position had become redundant.“Owing to certain ongoing organizational changes that are taking place in the company and after careful consideration of our current business needs, a decision has been taken to streamline operations. As a result, unfortunately the position you currently hold has become redundant. We want to assure you that this decision has been taken after thoughtful deliberation and has become inevitable in light of the need to restructure the business,” the note said.Affected employees are eligible for a severance package; HR will provide separation documents, package details, and other information on the next steps by email. They are also being relieved of their duties and placed on garden leave until their last date of employment, according to the communication.The severance package includes one month’s pay for every completed year of service, plus two additional months’ pay, according to sources.A junior developer who was among those affected wrote on Reddit that, while relieved not to have significant EMIs or loans, he had no backup plan. Being early in his career, the sudden job loss left him uncertain about what lay ahead.In fiscal 2026, Oracle cut 21,000 jobs globally and incurred $1.8 billion in severance costs, according to the company’s disclosures.
Article Summary: A viral Reddit post capturing the anxiety around the tech giant’s latest global layoffs simply read, “Time of death: 4 A.M. Lol” The employee said being logged out of Slack effectively confirmed the layoff. Oracle began a fresh round of layoffs in India on Monday.

Article Title: Rising crude, G-sec yields, inflation risks sink sensex
Article Text: Mumbai: With Brent firmly trading significantly above the psychologically important $100/barrel mark, US 10-year yield at two-decade high at over 5%, India 10-year at above 7.1%, and rupee weakening close to 96/$, Dalal Street investors pressed the panic button on Tuesday. As a result, sensex lost about 1,400 points from the day's high and closed 778 points or 1% down at 74,004 points, an over five-month low level. The rising retail inflation, partly due to rising crude prices, is also a concern for market players and investors.Tuesday's sell-off was more pronounced in small-cap and mid-cap stocks than in the large caps. This led to BSE's market cap plunging nearly Rs 9.2 lakh crore to settle at Rs 472.4 lakh crore, official data showed.The selling was led by foreign funds that net sold stocks worth nearly Rs 3,000 crore, while domestic funds were net buyers at almost Rs 2,700 crore, BSE data showed.According to Siddhartha Khemka, head of research - wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, Indian markets are likely to remain weak amid elevated crude prices, renewed inflation concerns and uncertainty ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision."Brent crude rose 2.3% to around $108/bbl amid unresolved geopolitical tensions and supply concerns, adding to inflationary pressures. Meanwhile, India's retail inflation accelerated to a 20-month high of 4.82% in Aug, raising concerns over the scope for further monetary easing and increasing expectations of a tighter RBI policy stance."The rising inflation and crude prices pushed the 10-year G-sec yield to 7.09%, a four-month high, further raising concerns over a tighter domestic rate environment, Khemka said.CAS effect: Nifty plunges 463 points in one minuteDuring the closing auction session (CAS) on Tuesday, the day Nifty weekly contracts expired, the index lost about 460 points (2%) in just one minute, between 3.20pm and 3.21pm, but soon recovered to eventually settle the session with a 280-point loss at 23,119 points. While the recently introduced CAS has resulted in substantial volatility in stock prices and some of the leading indices, the volatility has been more pronounced on days derivatives contracts--weekly and monthly--expired. TNN
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 2.3% to around $108/bbl amid unresolved geopolitical tensions and supply concerns, adding to inflationary pressures. India's retail inflation accelerated to a 20-month high of 4.82% in Aug, raising concerns over the scope for further monetary easing.

Article Title: At 26%, exports grow fastest in over 4 years
Article Text:
Trade deficit at 5-month low

New Delhi: Goods exports jumped over 26% to $43.8 billion, the fastest pace of expansion since June 2022, due to a surge in electronics, engineering goods and petroleum products, while lower gold shipments helped moderate import growth to 14%, and narrow the trade deficit to $26.9 billion, a five-month low.Latest data released by the commerce department on Tuesday pegged imports in Aug at $70.7 billion, compared with $62 billion a year ago."We have not just continued but improved upon the export growth in Aug... During the five months, imports are being propelled by strong domestic economic expansion, rising energy requirements and the critical inputs needed to sustain the rapid growth of the manufacturing sector," commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told reporters.Describing the data as robust, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said: "These numbers reaffirm the growing strength and competitiveness of our manufacturing ecosystem, with our exporters expanding India's footprint across global markets."Services too are estimated to have done well, with exports rising 24.7% to almost $39 billion, while imports were 37% higher at $21.4 billion.Agrawal said that during the first five months of the fiscal, export of goods and services was near the $400 billion mark.In rupee terms, exports saw a more rapid growth, which was the impact of the depreciation of the Indian currency, but Agrawal said that multiple factors were at play and not just a weaker currency. He also said that the expansion was driven by an increase in volumes in around 40% of the major product categories with several seeing value and volume growth.In Aug, petroleum exports jumped 63% to $6.8 billion. Engineering goods were up 25% at $12.3 billion, while electronics shipments soared almost 90% to $5.6 billion. On the import front, gold shipments fell 58% to $2.3 billion, while silver more than doubled to $1 billion. Along with electronics, whose imports jumped over 40% to $13.7 billion in Aug, and petroleum, silver accounted for the entire $8.5 billion increase in the import bill.
Article Summary: India's goods exports jumped over 26% to $43.8 billion, the fastest pace of expansion since June 2022. Lower gold shipments helped moderate import growth to 14%, and narrow the trade deficit to $26.9 billion. Latest data released by the commerce department on Tuesday pegged imports in Aug at $70.7 billion.

Article Title: Top banks to get lion's share of UPI fees
Article Text:
How much will they get

Mumbai: Banks with the largest number of bank accounts will be the biggest gainers as they will receive the lion's share of the fees. While third-party payment apps will receive a smaller share, the MDR will make the biggest difference to them as their business model suddenly becomes sustainable without having to look for alternative revenue streams.Using debit cards as a proxy for savings accounts, SBI is the clear leader with a 25% market share, followed by Bank of Baroda (8%), HDFC Bank (6.2%), Canara Bank (5.9%) and Union Bank (5.6%). For every Rs 2,000 paid, the merchant will pay Rs 8 as fees. Of this the issuing bank (from whose account money will be paid) will get Rs 3.2 as fees, while the bank that receives the payment (the acquiring bank) will get Rs 2.4 . Of the remaining Rs 2.4, the third-party app - PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm, Amazon Pay or WhatsApp - will get Rs 1.6 and the bank doing the processing for the app will get 80 paise.For banks, the deal gets even sweeter. The third-party payment apps will also pay a portion of their earnings to the banks that process the transactions. The processing bank (the bank whose name appears on the UPI ID) will get a share, as will the bank processing the transaction on the merchant end. Banks also pay a small interchange fee to the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).In all, the fee kitty would have to be divided among seven participants - the banks where the customer and shopkeeper have accounts, the banks processing transactions at both ends, the third-party apps and the network provider, NPCI.. "The sector has long been viewed as one where scale has been built without a clear path to monetisation. A sustainable revenue model for UPI would alter that perception, improve investor sentiment and give the fintech ecosystem a significant boost," said Amrish Rau, CEO, Pine Labs.
Article Summary: Banks with the largest number of bank accounts will be the biggest gainers as they will receive the lion's share of the fees. For every Rs 2,000 paid, the merchant will pay Rs 8 as fees. The third-party payment apps will also pay a portion of their earnings to the banks that process the transactions.

Article Title: EPFO has an official WhatsApp channel for PF updates; here’s how to join and get educational information on EPF advance withdrawals and more
Article Text:

How to join EPFO WhatsApp channel

Other EPFO awareness and service-related videos

Many banks offer WhatsApp services

How EPF WhatsApp service will work

The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has been taking steps to keep members informed and allow access for more information digitally. As part of this effort, the retirement fund body has asked members to follow its official WhatsApp channel for the latest updates and useful information concerning their provident fund accounts.The EPFO, in a social media post on X (formerly Twitter), said that members who join the WhatsApp channel can stay informed about the organisation’s latest updates.In its post on X, the EPFO said, “Join EPFO's official WhatsApp Channel to get important updates and useful information. Click on the link to join.”Members can access the official EPFO WhatsApp channel by using the link provided by the organisation.Members can join the EPFO’s official WhatsApp channel through the following link: https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb6kmH48Pgs8ftd6Kw3YBesides sharing updates, the EPFO WhatsApp channel also provides members with educational content through useful links. These include YouTube videos covering topics such as EPF advance withdrawals, EPF contributions after an employee rejoins employment and the payment process under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana.Types of educational links shared by the EPFO on WhatsAppThe EPFO’s official website provides members with information about several services, including EPF Advance, EPF withdrawal, UAN activation, claims and transfers, KYC, and pension-related facilities.The EPF scheme provides retirement savings along with tax-free interest growth, contributions from the employer and financial security for the family. Among its key features are a 12% contribution rate, online access to the EPF passbook, convenient transfer of accounts, nomination facilities and options to withdraw funds.Several banks in India have introduced WhatsApp-based services through which customers can securely perform tasks such as checking account balances, downloading statements, managing cards and requesting various services at any time. To use these facilities, customers generally need to send a 'Hi' from the mobile number registered with their bank.In May, the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) was reportedly working on plans to introduce its services through WhatsApp.A PTI report, citing Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, said the EPFO intended to use WhatsApp because of the messaging platform’s widespread use among mobile phone users across the country.Under the proposed system, EPFO members would be able to initiate a conversation with the organisation by sending a 'Hello' message to its verified WhatsApp number, which would carry a green tick.Members would also be able to receive updates related to the EPFO directly on their registered mobile numbers. According to the report, the service would support local and regional languages, allowing users to communicate in a language they are more comfortable with.Earlier this year, EPFO streamlined its partial PF withdrawal framework by consolidating 13 separate provisions into three broad categories: Essential Needs, Housing Needs and Special Circumstances.Under the revised rules, members can withdraw up to 100% of their eligible PF balance, while the withdrawal limits for education and marriage have also been increased. The minimum service requirement has been reduced to 12 months.Another key change is that members can seek a withdrawal under the ‘Special Circumstances’ category without having to provide a reason. The reform is intended to enable 100% auto-settlement of eligible claims, while keeping 25% of the PF balance invested for retirement.At present, members have to submit withdrawal applications, which can sometimes result in delays. With the auto-settlement facility, however, eligible withdrawal claims are processed electronically without manual intervention. Once the application is filed, subscribers can receive the money within three days.The EPFO has also raised the limit under the auto-settlement facility to Rs 5 lakh from Rs 1 lakh. The facility allows subscribers to access their funds within three days for requirements including marriage, education, illness and housing.
Article Summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has been taking steps to keep members informed and allow access for more information digitally. As part of this effort, the retirement fund body has asked members to follow its official WhatsApp channel for the latest updates and useful information.

Article Title: National Engineers' Day 2026: Meet A. Lalitha, India’s first female engineer who defied a male-dominated profession
Article Text:
A Lalitha, India’s first female engineer, broke barriers by pursuing engineering while raising her daughter as a young widow. (Image credits- All Together)

A young mother who refused to give up on education

She entered a college filled with men and etched her name on the leaves of history

From railway workshops to major engineering projects

Lalitha’s work on Bhakra Nangal Dam

She took India’s women engineers to the global stage

A legacy that began with one woman refusing to step back

Engineering has always been connected with males and has remained a male-dominated segment. Remember that dialogue from 3 Idiots? “Beta hua to engineer aur beti hui to doctor.” No matter how much we preach about gender equality, deep down, we have all witnessed the ever-existent and deeply rooted patriarchy that our society carries forth. But we are saying this in 2026. And a girl in the 1900s unshackled all the barriers and chose an unconventional path. Ayyalasomayajula Lalitha, born in 1919 in Madras, etched her name as one of the first female engineers of India.As it is well said by some, “We think it to be impossible until it is made possible by someone.” And hence, we always owe these trailblazers a lot. They opened the doors and left the footprints for their predecessors to follow. Lalitha’s journey was not an aisle of roses; it was filled with personal loss, determination, and an unshakable commitment to education. But her story is not merely about being the first woman to earn an engineering degree in India. It is about how she opened a door that had barely existed for women.A Lalitha was born on August 27, 1919, into a Telugu-speaking family in Madras, now Chennai. She was married at the age of 15 and gave birth to her daughter, Syamala, in 1937.Just four months after her daughter’s birth, Lalitha lost her husband. At an age when her life could easily have been defined by circumstance, Lalitha chose education instead. With the support of her father, Pappu Subba Rao, who was himself a professor at the College of Engineering, Guindy, she completed her secondary education and decided to pursue engineering. At that time, engineering colleges in India were overwhelmingly male-dominated.Lalitha joined the College of Engineering, Guindy, to study electrical engineering. She was the only woman among hundreds of male students.Yet, according to her daughter, the environment at the college was more supportive than one might expect. The administration arranged separate hostel accommodation for Lalitha, while fellow students ensured that she did not feel isolated.Lalitha was not entirely alone in breaking the gender barrier. P.K. Thressia and Leelamma Koshie, née George, were also studying engineering at the institution around the same period.In 1943, Lalitha graduated with a degree in electrical engineering, becoming India’s first woman engineer.Her education did not end with a degree. She undertook a one-year apprenticeship at the Jamalpur Railway Workshop, gaining practical exposure to engineering work in one of the country’s major railway repair and overhaul facilities.After completing her training, Lalitha worked with the Central Standards Organisation in Shimla. She also assisted her father with research involving smokeless ovens and an electrical musical instrument known as the jelectromonium.She subsequently spent a year in the electrical department of the East Indian Railways before joining the Indian government's Office of the Electrical Commissioner as a technical assistant.In 1948, she took another major step in her career when she joined Associated Electrical Industries (AEI), a British engineering firm in Calcutta.Her work there would place her on one of independent India’s most ambitious infrastructure projects.At AEI, Lalitha worked on the Bhakra Nangal Dam project, one of the country's landmark engineering undertakings.Her responsibilities included designing transmission lines and substation layouts. The work demanded technical expertise at a time when women engineers were still an extreme rarity in India.She remained associated with AEI, which was later taken over by the General Electric Company, for nearly three decades. She retired in 1977 after a long professional career.For Lalitha, engineering was not simply a profession through which she had broken a gender barrier. It became a field in which she built a sustained body of work.Lalitha's contribution extended beyond her professional assignments.In 1953, the Council of the Institution of Electrical Engineers in London elected her as an associate member. She was later promoted to full membership in 1966.In 1964, she became the only female engineer from India to attend the First International Conference of Women Engineers and Scientists in New York.The following year, she was elected a member of the British Women's Engineering Society.Her international engagement also had a wider purpose. As India's representative on the organising committee for the Second International Conference of Women Engineers and Scientists, held in Cambridge in 1967, Lalitha helped ensure that five Indian women were able to attend the conference.Her achievement, therefore, was not confined to becoming the first. She also worked to make sure that more women could follow.Lalitha never remarried after her husband's death. Her sister-in-law helped raise her daughter, Syamala, who later earned degrees in science and became a mathematics teacher.Lalitha died on October 12, 1979, at the age of 60 after suffering a brain aneurysm. But she left this abode, leaving an indelible mark on the hearts of young generations. Her story inherently carries forth not only a powerful lesson but also an emotion that being first is pivotal, but making the path easier for those who will follow is a greater achievement. Today, on National Engineers' Day, let us remember and pay our tributes to all those ingenous minds who walked with a beacon of light and knocked on the doors that were otherwise closed.
Article Summary: Ayyalasomayajula Lalitha, born in 1919 in Madras, etched her name as one of the first female engineers of India. She was married at the age of 15 and gave birth to her daughter, Syamala, in 1937. At that time, engineering colleges in India were overwhelmingly male-dominated. Her education did not end with a degree. She undertook a one-year apprenticeship at the Jamalpur Railway Workshop, gaining practical exposure to engineering.

Article Title: BJP wins but independents rewrite Rajasthan civic poll math
Article Text:
CM Bhajan Lal Sharma, BJP state president Madan Rathore and senior party functionaries celebrate at BJP headquarters in Jaipur Monday

Rajasthan civic poll

Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, BJP state President Madan Rathore and other leaders celebrate after the party's victory in the state local body elections at the BJP headquarter in Jaipur on 14 September 2026.





JAIPUR: Independents emerged as the decisive force in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections, limiting BJP ’s gains and keeping Congress competitive across several towns.BJP finished as the single largest party, but the scale of independent victories turned many civic bodies into arenas for post-poll negotiation rather than clear mandates.According to final figures uploaded on the State Election Commission website, results had been declared in 10,235 of 10,244 wards by late Monday, with BJP winning 4,179, Congress 3,613 and independents picking up 2,273 to collectively take third position and establish themselves as potential kingmakers in urban local bodies where neither major party managed to cross the majority mark.At the urban local body level, BJP secured majorities in four municipal corporations – Jaipur, Bhilwara, Kota and Udaipur – and emerged as the single largest party in Alwar. Of the 47 municipal councils, BJP won a clear majority in 11, Congress in six and independents or others in four. In Fatehpur, Congress was tied with an independent candidate.The results give BJP the numerical edge, but not the sweep it sought in the first major statewide urban electoral test for the Bhajan Lal Sharma govt since it came to power in Dec 2023. Sharma campaigned extensively, holding roadshows in Ajmer, Bhilwara, Udaipur, Pali, Bikaner, Bharatpur, Jaipur, Alwar, Jodhpur and Kota.Even so, the party suffered reverses in key pockets and fell short in several prestige contests.The sharpest setbacks came from politically symbolic terrain.Jhalawar and Baran, former chief minister Vasundhara Raje’s strongholds for four decades, slipped out of BJP’s control. Congress won Jhalawar, while AAP made its political debut in the state by claiming control of its maiden municipal body in Baran.Sharma also faced a difficult verdict in his home turf of Bharatpur despite his direct role in candidate selection. Independents won 36 wards there, compared with 20 for BJP and seven for Congress, leaving the ruling party far from a majority.Pali delivered another blow. BJP lost the city to Congress despite its association with BJP state president Madan Rathore, cabinet minister Joraram Kumawat and former Union minister PP Choudhary.The party also suffered setbacks in parts of Shekhawati and eastern Rajasthan. Its performance in Bikaner and Ajmer, where Congress ended BJP’s 36-year hold over the city, has sharpened concerns within the organisation, particularly with panchayat polls likely later this year.Congress, though behind BJP in the overall tally, gained enough ground to make the point that BJP’s urban dominance remained incomplete. State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra delivered a strong result for the party in his home turf of Sikar and Laxmangarh, strengthening his position within the state unit.In Tonk, Congress managed an edge in Sachin Pilot’s political turf even though the former deputy chief minister largely stayed away from campaigning and ticket distribution. The party also mounted a serious challenge in Jodhpur, former chief minister Ashok Gehlot’s political base, where Union minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat campaigned extensively over the past month.The CPM also entered the winners’ list by commanding enough numbers to form the board in Nokha, Bikaner.The strongest signal from the verdict is the independent vote. With 2,273 wards, independents are set to influence control in several bodies where neither BJP nor Congress has a clear majority. Their performance points to the continuing strength of local networks, candidate reputation and ward-level grievances over party loyalty in many towns.The State Election Commission Monday postponed, until further orders, elections for chairperson and deputy chairperson in four urban local bodies after technical glitches in EVMs delayed the declaration of results. The affected bodies include Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota municipal corporations, and Suket municipality in Kota. During counting, results from some booths could not be released due to EVM malfunctions, leaving the results in these bodies incomplete. The Commission said fresh dates would be announced later.The SEC has ordered repolling at 10 polling stations in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota and Suket. Repolling will be held on Sept 16 from 7am to 6pm, with counting on Sept 17 from 8am at designated centres.The affected booths include five in Jaipur Municipal Corporation, one in Jodhpur Municipal Corporation, three in Kota Municipal Corporation and one in Suket municipality. The Commission said the number of votes affected by the malfunction exceeded the victory margins between the nearest rival candidates, requiring repolling.In Jaipur, BJP crossed the majority mark with 78 seats in the 150-member Jaipur Municipal Corporation. Results of four wards were withheld after EVMs developed technical snags, leaving counting incomplete.Elections were held in two phases, on Sept 9 and 11, across 309 urban local bodies — 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipalities. The increase in the number of bodies since the previous elections followed the creation of new municipalities, expansion and reorganisation of existing urban areas, and delimitation.The results mark a shift from the map that emerged after the previous municipal elections, held between Nov 2019 and Feb 2021, when Rajasthan had 196 urban local bodies with 7,500 wards. After the election of mayors and chairpersons, Congress controlled 123 bodies, BJP 64, and Independents and other parties nine.
Article Summary: BJP finished as the single largest party, but scale of independent victories turned many civic bodies into arenas for post-poll negotiation. Results had been declared in 10,235 of 10,244 wards by late Monday. BJP won a clear majority in 11, Congress in six and independents or others in four.

Article Title: Oil price today: Brent crude rises as Saudi pipeline outage, fresh attacks raise supply concerns
Article Text:
The rise in oil prices added to inflation concerns.

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Tuesday as concerns over global supplies intensified after attacks disrupted Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and planned talks between Gulf Arab states and Iran were postponed.Brent crude futures gained $1.24, or 1.18%, to $106.93 a barrel at 0026 GMT, after rising 1% in the previous session. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures climbed $1.29, or 1.24%, to $102.65 a barrel, following a 1.3% increase on Monday.Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia on Monday, targeting the Khamis Mushait military airbase in the country’s south.The Houthis said the missile and drone attack was carried out in retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen. The assault reportedly targeted aircraft hangars, radar systems, runways and ammunition depots.The latest attack followed strikes on Friday that Riyadh blamed on Iran-backed fighters in Iraq. Those attacks disrupted Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, which allows the kingdom to transport oil to the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz.Saudi Arabia uses the pipeline to reroute around four million barrels of oil per day to the port of Yanbu.The outage could remove as much as 4% of global oil supply from the market if operations are not restored, according to Saudi buyers and traders.Shipping concerns also deepened after commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to fewer than 10 transits a day over the weekend, compared with a 10-day average of 14.The waterway carried nearly one-fifth of global oil supplies before the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28. Gulf Arab states also postponed planned discussions with Iran, adding to concerns that the regional conflict could widen and further disrupt energy shipments.The rise in oil prices added to inflation concerns and pushed benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields to 5% overnight—their highest level since October 2023. The yield later eased to 4.9895%.Asian shares remained subdued as investors assessed Middle East tensions, higher oil prices and elevated bond yields ahead of key central bank meetings in the United States and Japan.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 0.12%, while South Korea’s benchmark declined 0.25%. Japan’s Nikkei edged up 0.19% after recovering from early losses.The Bank of Japan is widely expected to raise its interest rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% at the end of its two-day meeting on Friday and signal further tightening.In currency markets, the dollar index rose 0.05% to 99.53. The dollar gained 0.17% against the yen to 154.61, while the euro slipped 0.03% to $1.1543. Spot gold fell 0.15% to $4,291.59 an ounce, while silver declined 0.31% to $63.03.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures gained $1.24, or 1.18%, to $106.93 a barrel at 0026 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures climbed 1.24% to $102.65 a barrel, following a 1.3% increase on Monday.

Article Title: From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape
Article Text:
From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

From discarded tyres to footwear with a purpose, the idea began with a childhood experience. At the age of 10, UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar visited rural Africa, where he saw children walking long distances barefoot, often without adequate footwear.Moved by what he witnessed, Ahaan gave away his favourite pair of slippers to a child he met during the visit. The experience stayed with him long after he returned home and eventually became the starting point for a larger idea.As he grew older, Ahaan began exploring how discarded materials could be repurposed to address the lack of affordable, durable footwear. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles.The idea brought together two concerns he had encountered separately: the growing problem of tyre waste and the need for accessible footwear.He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala, and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day. Ahaan then connected with Mamco General Trading, which operates in Uganda and Zambia. As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility programme, the company will purchase 4,000 pairs of slippers each month for free distribution to children and families in need. It’s a sustainable cycle that turns waste into opportunity, supporting livelihoods and giving kids durable footwear.“When I was 10 years old, I saw children my age walking barefoot, and I never forgot that moment,” Ahaan says. “I wanted to create something that could help people and the environment. If we can turn discarded tyres into something useful and long-lasting, maybe it can inspire more young people to believe their simple ideas can really make a difference.”The world’s growing dependence on convenience and mobility comes with an environmental cost. Every year, more than a billion tyres reach the end of their usable life, creating a significant waste-management challenge. Many of these tyres end up in landfills, while others are burned or processed in ways that can contribute to pollution and the loss of valuable materials.Repurposing discarded tyres offers one way to address this challenge by keeping materials in use for longer and reducing the amount of waste that needs to be disposed of. Turning old tyres into durable slipper soles, for instance, gives a material that would otherwise be discarded a new application while also reducing the need for virgin raw materials in footwear production.The approach reflects a broader shift in how sustainability is being understood. Rather than treating waste simply as something to be collected and discarded, initiatives like this explore how materials already in circulation can be redesigned and put to practical use.In doing so, they can support waste reduction, resource conservation and efforts to lower the environmental impact associated with new production. Ultimately, sustainability is not only about recycling what has already been used, but also about rethinking waste as a potential resource.
Article Summary: UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar saw children walking barefoot in rural Africa. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles. He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day.

Article Title: Global AI stocks slide as warnings over rapid development trigger investor concerns
Article Text:
AI stocks tumble as debt, valuations and slowing development fears hit market (representative image)

Amodei calls for slower AI development

AI investment faces fresh questions

Investors remain divided

AI-linked stocks across global markets plunged on Monday after leaders of some of the world’s biggest artificial intelligence companies called for a slower pace of development, raising fresh questions over the huge investments that have driven the sector’s rally.The warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI chief Elon Musk, added to scrutiny of an AI industry that is increasingly relying on debt and circular financing while raising spending forecasts.Nasdaq e-mini futures fell 1.9%, with chip stocks among the biggest decliners. Nvidia fell 3%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 5.7% and SpaceX fell 2.6%. Meta and Amazon declined more than 1.4% each.In Europe, technology stocks fell 2.5%, with chip equipment maker ASML down 5.8%, Infineon falling 8.4% and Siemens Energy losing 7.4%.Asian AI-linked stocks also came under pressure. SoftBank fell as much as 13.2%, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company declined 1.2% and South Korea’s SK Hynix dropped 6.3%.Amodei, in an essay shared on X on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the pace at which they improve the capabilities of their models, citing growing concerns over potential misuse and the difficulty of controlling increasingly powerful systems.He warned that within six to 12 months, AI agents “could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.”Anthropic had also released a threat intelligence report detailing the use of its Claude AI models in activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon subsequently resigned, saying the companies developing frontier AI were moving too quickly.“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon said.Altman has backed Amodei’s call for greater caution, while also confirming that OpenAI would not proceed with an initial public offering this year, citing safety concerns. He said the risks of human extinction posed by AI were “unacceptable”.Musk also endorsed Amodei’s position, writing: “Dario is right.”The warnings have raised concerns about whether the extraordinary spending on AI infrastructure can continue if the pace of technological development slows.“If the AI race slows materially, the key question becomes: who pays for all that infrastructure?” said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote.“The leases, debt and power commitments remain even if expected compute demand and revenue growth slow. And that could bring credit risk increasingly into the AI story,” she added.AI-related stocks have powered a significant part of global equity gains since OpenAI launched ChatGPT in 2022. However, concerns over cyberattacks involving AI agents and public opposition to data-centre construction have added to scrutiny of the industry.Despite the latest warnings, Morgan Stanley’s Brian Nowak expects AI spending to exceed $1.2 trillion by 2027.Deutsche Bank said the competitive race between companies and countries remained intense and that it was difficult to imagine firms voluntarily slowing down while rivals continued to advance.Some investors dismissed the warnings. Michael Burry, known for betting against the US housing market before the 2008 financial crisis, described the warnings as “hype and puffery” and “cover for real uncontrollable slowing growth”.Others said the warnings could still weigh on AI and semiconductor stocks in the short term because valuations depend on strong demand and continued technological progress.“Their valuations assume both strong demand and a relentless pace of technological progress,” said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore, as quoted by Reuters.“When expectations are this high, even a possible delay can trigger profit-taking.”The market sell-off also came as oil prices rose amid concerns over global energy supplies.Brent crude rose more than 3% to around $108.74 a barrel after Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline following an attack.US markets were also facing pressure from higher energy prices and rising Treasury yields, while investors were monitoring the Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting.Meanwhile, the US and Chinese governments are expected to hold AI safety talks this month as part of broader bilateral discussions, according to two people briefed on the plans.
Article Summary: Nasdaq e-mini futures fell 1.9%, with chip stocks among the biggest decliners. Nvidia fell 3%, Advanced Micro Devices dropped 5.7% and SpaceX fell 2.6%. Meta and Amazon declined more than 1.4% each.

Article Title: Oil prices jump over 2%: Brent tops $107 as fresh Saudi, Strait of Hormuz strikes fuel supply fears
Article Text:
Brent crude climbs.

Oil prices rose more than 2% on Monday as fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iranian strikes on vessels in the Gulf added to supply concerns following the shutdown of a key Saudi oil pipeline.Brent crude futures rose $2.90, or 2.77%, to $107.51 a barrel by 2313 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $2.27, or 2.27%, to $102.32 a barrel.Prices had initially climbed more than 3% at the market open. Brent rose $3.62, or 3.46%, to $108.23 a barrel by 2214 GMT on Sunday, while WTI increased $3.15, or 3.15%, to $103.20 a barrel.Saudi state media on Sunday released footage showing damage to homes and a mosque in the southern Jazan province following what it described as a Houthi attack. The Iran-aligned Houthis also said they had targeted a Saudi military base in a neighbouring province.Separately, a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile, causing a fire and forcing its crew to evacuate, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said.Iran said one person was killed and four crew members were wounded after an Iranian commercial vessel was struck off the country’s coast.Oil prices were expected to rise after Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline was shut on Friday following a drone attack originating in Iraq.The pipeline allows Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest oil exporter, to reroute shipments and avoid the Strait of Hormuz. Its shutdown threatens up to 4% of global oil supply.Meanwhile, Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim on Friday, tightening their position near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another key oil transit route that has carried 4-5% of global supply in recent months.Oil prices have risen around 8% over the past week, crossing $100 a barrel for the first time since July, as escalating tensions in the Middle East raised concerns over global supplies.The Strait of Hormuz remained at the centre of the confrontation. Nearly one-fifth of the world’s oil passed through the strategic waterway before the war began, with both the United States and Iran seeking to exert control over it.Oman postponed a scheduled meeting with Iran and other regional countries on Monday to discuss the management of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Omani foreign minister Badr Albusaidi said on X that the meeting had been postponed “in the interests of consensus”. Mohammad Ali Bak, an official in Iran’s foreign ministry quoted by IRNA, said the talks were postponed “at the request of some regional countries”.The meeting was expected to focus on efforts by Iran and Oman, which lies on the other side of the strait, to manage shipping through the key waterway.No peace talks have taken place in the war, which began six months ago with US and Israeli strikes, since an interim agreement reached in June collapsed after a few weeks.
